- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–5% above recent peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 72+ to 68–70), reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.4+ values), model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5–7 days are consistently above true outcome, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days to avoid overconfidence bias.
